newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper goes on Asia trade tour.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper goes on Asia trade tour.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper departs on Friday for a whirlwind tour of Asia that will include official visits to China, Indonesia and South Korea.

Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia told reporters the trip, one of Samper's rare sojourns outside the Americas, was primarily aimed at boosting trade ties with Asia and opening it up as a market for Colombian exports.

China, especially, could eventually prove to be an important market for coffee, Mejia said, adding that the National Coffee Growers Federation was planning on opening two shops there to help stimulate demand for Colombian beans.
"If every Chinese were to drink a cup of coffee a month, China could consume the 12 million (60-kilo) bags of coffee we produce yearly," Mejia said.
Chinese-Colombian trade is currently valued at just $1.5 million per year, but Mejia said Samper hoped to increase the trade flow between the two countries substantially.

In addition to Mejia, Samper will be accompanied on his trip by Foreign Trade Minister Morris Harf, a large delegation of private sector businessmen and representatives of Colombia's state oil and coal companies.
Samper's first stopover, in China, will mark the first visit ever to that country by a Colombian head of state.

After stopovers in Beijing and Shanghai, and an obligatory visit to the Great Wall, Samper will depart for Jakarta, where he is scheduled to arrive on Wednesday for a one-day visit. He then flies to South Korea, where he will pay homage to the Colombians who fought alongside Americans in the Korean War.
Samper will head home on Saturday, Oct. 26, with scheduled layovers in Sapporo, Japan, and Vancouver, Canada, for refueling of the presidential jet.

The jet, a Boeing 707, was at the centre of a scandal last month when more than eight pounds (3.7 kg) of heroin were found stashed aboard it as it was being readied for Samper's visit to U.N. headquarters in New York.

Samper's nine-day absence from Colombia, after he hands over power to Interior Minister Horacio Serpa on Friday, will mark his longest departure from the Casa de Narino presidential palace since he took office in August 1994.
